p01.why: Each later declaration adds a default from the right, so f() is f(1, 2), which is 12.

p02.why: operator+ must not have a default argument.

p03.why: The local appears only in sizeof, an operand that is not evaluated.

p04.why: The name limit in the default means the global seen at the declaration, so f() returns 3.

p05.why: A parameter pack and an ellipsis can follow a parameter with a default, and the values match the assertions.

p06.why: A default argument must not use this.

p07.why: The default reads the current value of value, 5, at the call.

p08.why: The block declaration has its own default 7, so f() inside g calls f(7).

p09.why: 1.5 is not a valid initializer for int*, and the default is checked at the declaration.

p10.why: The packs count their arguments, and after_default uses its default before a pack, so all assertions hold.

p11.why: The missing trailing arguments take the defaults 2 and 3.

p12.why: b follows a parameter with a default and has none.

p13.why: The default comes from a later declaration and is used through an earlier using declaration; GCC and EDG accept, and Clang rejects.

p14.why: A pointer to a function cannot have default arguments.

p15.why: The parameter a appears only in sizeof.

p16.why: The inline function has different defaults in the two units, which needs no diagnostic; the program accepts either value and exits 0.

p17.why: An ellipsis can follow a parameter with a default argument.

p18.why: A call through a pointer must give every argument.

p19.why: The default for a is given again, even with the same value.

p20.why: The default for a is given again.

p21.why: next() runs at each call that uses the default, giving 1 and 2, and f(10) does not call it.

p22.why: A default argument uses a local of the enclosing function in an evaluated operand.

p23.why: A default argument uses another parameter in an evaluated operand.
